summary:
Prince Edward Island stands under the national framework of Canada. The province's own instruments govern gender-marker changes on provincial documents and driver's licences.

In April 2016 the MacLauchlan government tabled a bill amending the Vital Statistics Act so that an Islander can change the gender recorded on official provincial documents by declaring the gender they identify with and providing a letter from a doctor. Sex-reassignment surgery ceased to be required, and the province's gender-marker change has operated without a surgery requirement since that amendment.

Since 4 December 2018 Islanders identifying gender on a driver's licence may select 'gender not listed', shown on the licence as X, or 'prefer not to say', shown as a blank, alongside male and female. The Government of Prince Edward Island states this made the province the first jurisdiction in Canada to offer the 'prefer not to say' blank option; provincial photo ID issued at Access PEI locations can therefore carry an X or a blank gender marker.

Under the province's published process, an adult may apply for a change of gender designation if born in Prince Edward Island and resident in the province for at least three months and not in the lawful custody of another person. The application requires completed forms including a physician statement and a written statement by the applicant, with signatures arranged before a commissioner of oaths at Vital Statistics.
tangentialFactors:
The source inventory records no Prince Edward Island-specific hate-crime rate or incident count. Statistics Canada's release of 30 March 2026 on police-reported hate crime for 2024 gives national figures only, and no provincially deviating pattern for Prince Edward Island is documented.

Advocacy for a third gender category has been voiced from within the province but is not law: a Pride P.E.I. board member welcomed the 2016 amendment while calling for a future third gender category, noting that many people he knew in Charlottetown identify outside the binary.
localsOnly:
The change-of-gender-designation route is resident-facing: it requires at least three months of provincial residence and, for a person born elsewhere, is not available on the terms published by the province as captured on 1 July 2022.

For a minor under 18 born in Prince Edward Island and resident in the province for at least three months, a legal custodian may apply, with written consent of any other custodian or parent and of the child if aged 12 or older.

A linked item on the CBC article page of 18 April 2016 reports that Health PEI would cover the costs of three surgeries for transgender patients. The record does not state whether that coverage has continued, been expanded, or ended.
outOfScopeNotes:
Unresolved: the inventory contains no Prince Edward Island-specific hate-crime figure, no trans-specific violence count for the province, and no documented enforcement or complaint outcome under the province's gender-marker rules. The absence of a provincial figure in the national release is not evidence of a low or high rate.

Not sourced: whether Access PEI or other provincial counters have documented practices for handling gender-marker discrepancies between a visitor's federal passport and provincial photo ID, and whether any provincial facility policy governs sex-segregated spaces, is not addressed anywhere in the inventory.

Not sourced: the current status of the third gender category advocated in 2016. No later provincial instrument creating a non-binary marker on birth records or other vital documents appears in the record; the X and blank options documented here apply to driver's licences and provincial photo ID.
